title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page continues an explicit calculation in a profinite fundamental groupoid (called 'VII-bar' on the previous page) whose base points are the two hemisphere centres P^+ and P^- of P^1(C) minus {0,1,infinity}, together with six points R_i^± near the punctures i = 0, 1, infinity. The generators are three families of arcs and loops: arcs d_i^ω: P^ω -> R_i^ω, arcs d'_i^ω, and loops/arcs a_i^ω: R_i^ω -> R_i^ω' around the punctures. The vertex group is \hat Π_{03}, the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points, which is free profinite on two generators. The symmetric group S_3 acts on it through automorphisms written ε_0, σ_∞ (involutions) and ρ (order 3).

The ansatz. An automorphism u of the groupoid (meant to be a Galois element, or an element of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group) is described by its values on the generators (formula 73). These values are given by three parameters ξ', ξ_1, λ in \hat Π_{03}: u(d) is d twisted by ξ_1, u(d') is d' twisted by ξ', and u(a) = a·φ(λ). The task is to translate the defining relations (72) of the groupoid into equations on (λ, ξ', ξ_1).

Step 1. The first relation (72a) gives ξ' = ε_0(λ ξ_1), i.e. ξ_1 = λ^{-1} ε_0^{-1}(ξ'). This eliminates ξ_1.

Step 2. The auxiliary quantity β' (introduced at (75)) is computed three ways:
- β' = ξ_1 σ_∞(ξ')^{-1};
- β' = ξ_1 (σ_∞ ε_0)(λ ξ_1)^{-1};
- β' = λ^{-1} ε_0^{-1}(ξ') σ_∞(ξ')^{-1}.

Step 3. Applying σ_∞ (using σ_∞^2 = 1 and ρ = σ_∞ ε_0^{-1}) gives σ_∞(β') = σ_∞(λ)^{-1} ρ(ξ') ξ'^{-1}. Equivalently, (77): σ_∞(β')^{-1} = α' σ_∞(λ), with α' := ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}.

Step 4. The second relation (72b), a hexagon-like loop through both hemispheres, is equivalent to the 2-cycle-type identity (78): β' σ_∞(β') = 1, i.e. β' = σ_∞(β')^{-1}. Grothendieck observes the following:
- The condition is invariant under the substitution β' ↦ σ_∞(β')^{-1}.
- So β_1 := σ_∞(β')^{-1} = α' σ_∞(λ) satisfies the same equation β_1 σ_∞(β_1) = 1, and β_1 = β'.
- Hence one may simply set (79): β' = α' σ_∞(λ) = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1} σ_∞(λ).

Step 5 (completed on the next page). The only remaining condition on (λ, ξ') is that the β' of (79) equals the β' of (76)/(76'). Explicitly:
λ^{-1} ε_0^{-1}(ξ') σ_∞(ξ')^{-1} = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1} σ_∞(λ).

Purpose. This is the elimination of variables in the 'lego' description of the Galois action on the genus-0, 3-punctured piece of the Teichmüller tower. It reduces an automorphism of the S_3-symmetric groupoid to a pair (λ, ξ') subject to one relation of 2-cycle/3-cycle type. It is a groupoid-level precursor of Drinfeld's description of \hat{GT} by pairs (λ, f) satisfying the 2-, 3- and 5-cycle relations.
errors: No substantive error. The algebra checks provided σ_∞ is an involution and ρ = σ_∞ ∘ ε_0^{-1} as automorphisms of \hat Π_{03}; in a groupoid these hold only up to the transport/conjugation by the bracketed paths [-d-], which the page suppresses.

The β_1 argument is slightly circuitous. It amounts to: β σ_∞(β) = 1 iff β = σ_∞(β)^{-1}, so the equation determines β' from (77). Logically fine, but β' ↦ β'^{-1} is not literally a symmetry used in the conclusion.
Equation labels on the page are inconsistent: (75) vs (76), and a duplicate/crossed-out (77). The next page refers to (76), (76'), (77), (78), (79).

ideas.what: Describing a Galois/GT element by its action on a multi-base-point fundamental groupoid of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, with S_3-symmetric base points (hemisphere centres and points near the punctures), parametrized by group elements (λ, ξ', ξ_1).
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group acting on the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid ('lego', tangential base points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) in program form; Drinfeld 1990 and Ihara for the explicit \hat{GT}; groupoid versions by Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2, programmatic only; the explicit computations are not published

ideas.what: Elimination of parameters reducing the cocycle (hexagon-type) relation to β'σ_∞(β') = 1 with β' = ξ'ρ(ξ')^{-1}σ_∞(λ).
ideas.modern_name: 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 and the 3-cycle/hexagon relation for \hat{GT}

missed.claim: Explicit pre-Drinfeld manipulation of the 2-cycle-type relation (β σ_∞(β) = 1) for the Galois action on the groupoid of P^1 minus 3 points, with a parameter λ living in \hat Π_{03} (a group element twisting the loops a_i) rather than in \hat Z^*. This is a variant parametrization differing from Drinfeld's (λ, f); its relation to \hat{GT} is not worked out on the page.
missed.quote: En résumé, on peut donc de suite poser (79) β' = α'σ_∞(λ) où α' = ξ'ρ(ξ')^{-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is documentary evidence that Grothendieck derived GT-type defining relations explicitly, for the dual-hemisphere groupoid. It is of historical interest for crediting the GT relations. The mathematical content is essentially subsumed by Drinfeld/Ihara and later groupoid formulations.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine but explicit elimination computation. Its interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck explicitly deriving 2-cycle/hexagon-type relations in a groupoid setting, predating Drinfeld. The content itself is subsumed by known \hat{GT} theory.
transcription_corrections: The equation labelled (75) at the top is very likely (76), and (75') is (76'): the previous page already uses (75), and the next page cites (76), (76').
The crossed-out boxed passage was labelled (77) and reads roughly 'Ceci dit, l'équation pour (72 b) équivaut : β'σ_∞(β') = 1, soit, en posant β_1 = σ_∞(β') ...'.
The reference '(\*)' in 'compte tenu de (\*)' likely points to (77).
In the last displayed equation of the β_1 argument the left factor is β_1 (the image shows β_1/β_2 overwritten); the final label is (79), overwritten from (78).
